$comment: Art for things that live in a save rather than in data/: residents made in the character creator (by character id) and named pets (by owner id and name), plus pictures of places, the bus, the city and concept posters. Paths are relative to the livera folder. tests/test_cast.cpp checks that every path exists, that no resident here is a founding character (their art is linked from data/characters), that each pet key is owner:name with a real species, and that place and stop ids are the game's. Facts on the cards were checked against the game's data; anything the card gets wrong is listed under notes so nobody mistakes it for the game's state.

residents.$comment: Characters made in the creator whose art exists, by character id (sheet, avatar, card_title, notes). Empty since D-073: Kai Morgan, Rosa Delgado, Sol Rivera and Theo Grant, the four whose sheets were drawn from the town-preview recording, are data characters now and link their art from data/characters (profile.appearance.visual_reference, avatar, art_notes).

All seven stops now have a full shelter sprite (stops/<stop_id>.webp, isometric, golden hour, transparent, from PROMPT_PACK_TOWN.md); their `crop` is the earlier small panel from the bus collage. Church Street has two near-identical versions; Lexington Ave & River Rd's tree and planters are the picture's own. Founders Park's shelter and Lexington Ave's `alternate` came as one picture of two shelters side by side: each was cut out and scaled up 1.37x onto the same 1254 px frame as the Riverside Lofts shelter (the same design), so they are a little softer than the others.
The route diagram names the seven real stops in order and the real $2.75 fare; its geography (the river, the loop's shape, a 'Rivéra River') is stylised and not the game's coordinates.
The transit card is branding only: fares in the game are paid by card, cash or LivPay, and there is no transit-card item.
The side view is a crop on a grey studio background, not a transparent sprite.

The Founders Way & Main totem reads FOUNDERS WAY, as its prompt asked: the stop's name in the data is longer than a totem holds. Every totem's gold 1 is the line number, not the stop's place in the route.

bus_line_1_rear.webp is the rear three-quarter view (the rear and the left side): emerald livery, gold stripe, LIVÉRA TRANSIT and the 1 badge front and back, as asked. The client still draws its own shuttle on the map.

bus_line_1_front.webp is the front three-quarter view (the front and the right side with both doors): the destination sign reads 1 RIVERSIDE LOOP, LIVÉRA TRANSIT and the lotus along the side, the gold 1 badge, as asked. It came in one picture with the clinic and was cut out. The client still draws its own shuttle on the map.
Ground tiles, the crane and the bridge, made from the 'Ground tiles and the crane' prompts in PROMPT_PACK_TOWN.md: isometric, golden hour, transparent.

The flat tiles are 2:1 diamonds (1774x887). The web client's view is 30-degree isometric (about 1.73:1), so it re-projects a tile to a flat texture before drawing it; nothing in a tile is a fact about the town.
road_gravel_alt and road_crossroad_alt are squarer diamonds (about 1.37:1) from a first round; the 2:1 versions are the ones to use.
river_edge: a stone promenade with a black-and-gold railing and the water; no data file gives the river a shape (the sketch draws it along the east edge).
bridge: four arches, lamps and a stair at the near end. Like the river it is part of the sketch: no data file has a bridge and nobody can cross it in the game.
crane: the tower crane the client draws over every active construction project; it is a marker, not a count of real cranes.

road_t and road_corner_alt came as one picture and were split; both are about 1.65:1 diamonds rather than 2:1. road_corner_alt is a curved bend; the map's streets never bend, so neither is drawn yet (D-059).
Stages 2, 3 and 4 have no panorama yet. construction.jpg is a building site, not a city stage.

Concept posters only. Their districts (Riverfront, The Ridge, The Nine, The Meadows...), 'Riverview Park' and the street layout are not the game's; the real places and bus stops are in data/world and data/transit.
The moonlit salon and the gold mirror wall are unassigned interiors: no place in the data has been given them.
The laptop set (laptop, mouse, sleeve) is a product mock-up; only the laptop is an item.

interior_law_office.jpg is a mood reference for interiors (black marble, gold, warm lamps, a dusk skyline through the window; art/STYLE.md). The two people in it are not game characters: no founder is a lawyer and nobody in the cast has this sheet. The book spines (CORPORATE LAW, BLACK WOMEN IN LAW...) are the picture's own text. The skyline outside is the future city of the concept posters, not the founding town.
